Prepare for the customer conversation

A useful account brief is more than a company summary. It should tell the seller what the customer has said, what the team has committed to, what changed since the last meeting, and which facts remain uncertain. Those details often sit across a CRM record, correspondence, call notes, and a Slack thread.

Maia can assemble that context in the deal channel. Start with one account and identify the records it may use. Ask Maia to separate confirmed facts from open questions and suggestions. The result gives the seller a reviewable packet without hiding gaps behind a confident narrative.

Build a sourced account brief

Provide the current opportunity record, the most recent approved notes, relevant correspondence, and any named public sources needed for research. Set a time boundary so an old conversation does not look current. Ask for the customer's stated priorities, active stakeholders, previous commitments, current stage evidence, and questions to resolve on the next call.

Every important claim should point back to its source. If the CRM close date and a recent email disagree, Maia should show both rather than silently choose one. The account executive decides which date is valid and whether the CRM needs a change.

That distinction matters for web research too. A public announcement may help prepare a question, but it is not proof of a customer's internal plan. Maia can cite the page and label the inference. The seller decides whether it belongs in the conversation.

Review pipeline by exception

Pipeline meetings lose time when every opportunity receives the same summary. Give Maia your team's stage definitions, required fields, next-step rules, and an export of open opportunities. Ask it to find missing next steps, stale activity, dates that moved, or stage evidence that conflicts with the record.

The output can be a short queue with the reason each deal needs attention. It should not assign a predictive win rate or invent a forecast category. Sellers and managers retain the judgment to change the forecast, reset a date, close an opportunity, or decide that the existing record is correct.

For a recurring review, keep the source, field rules, date window, and channel audience fixed. A weekly exception list becomes useful when everyone knows why a record appears and can correct the rule in the thread.

Draft the follow-through

After a meeting, give Maia the approved notes, the relevant account context, and the collateral the seller is allowed to share. It can draft a concise follow-up that separates customer commitments from your team's actions. It can also propose the exact CRM fields that may need an update.

Treat those as two different artifacts. The email draft needs the seller's editorial review and explicit send. A CRM change needs its own supported action and approval. Keeping the change set visible prevents a helpful draft from becoming an unexamined system update.

Hand off without losing commitments

Sales and customer success need the same facts but use them for different decisions. Maia can prepare a handoff from the approved opportunity record, signed terms, meeting notes, and implementation commitments. The output should identify the customer's goal, promised dates, commercial boundaries, owners, and unresolved questions.

The relationship owner and delivery owner confirm that packet together. Maia can expose missing information, but it cannot decide what was contractually promised or assign work on behalf of the team.

Start with one account

Choose one account the seller knows well. Ask Maia for the brief, including one conflicting date and one missing stakeholder detail. The seller can resolve both in the thread, edit the follow-up, and decide whether the CRM needs a separate update.

Connected-app availability varies by setup. A supplied CRM export and email thread are enough to prepare the first brief. With connected apps, each person works within the access available to them, and the channel should have an appropriate audience for the retrieved information.

Questions from sales teams

Which CRMs can Maia connect to?

Confirm the exact CRM and operations available in your Maia setup. You can begin with an authorized export while your team validates a live connection.

Does Maia send emails or update opportunities on its own?

Start with drafts and proposed field changes. Sending a message and changing a CRM record are separate external actions that the seller should inspect and approve.

Can a manager run a team pipeline review?

Yes, when Maia has an approved set of opportunity records and your team's review rules. Choose a channel whose members may see the account information, and keep forecast judgment with the sales team.
